thread:
anna: Heads-up — noticed anomalous KV cache growth after last rollout. Mem used +22%, fragmentation higher, but prefix hit improvement negligible.
liam: Do we have the exact key derivation that changed?
anna: Yep. Previously:
```
// old
key = fmt("%s:prefix:%s", model, sha1(prefix))
```
Now we do per-tenant salt:
```
// new naive
key = fmt("%s:prefix:%s:%s", model, tenant_id, sha1(prefix))
```
liam: That explains duplication across tenants. We isolated collisions but lost inter-tenant reuse for common system prompts.
sylvia: Observed effects in profile: more unique entries, slower LRU churn, larger resident set. Long-lived chat sessions kept private copies of the same prefix for each tenant.
anna: Bench numbers from staging (20k sessions, mean seq 1400):
- baseline keying: prefix hit 51%, p95 latency 48ms, mem 1.1GB
- naive tenant-salt: prefix hit 52%, p95 52ms, mem 1.36GB
- dedupe-in-batcher: prefix hit 52%, p95 50ms, mem 1.28GB

runtime-bot: ALERT: perf-regression detector fired for eng-runtime 2023-12-03T21:07Z (+6% latency)
liam: Two directions: (A) restore global keying for non-sensitive namespaces; (B) keep isolation but add a canonicalization layer to collapse duplicate content.
sylvia: Canonicalization idea: maintain canonical_entry map keyed by content_fingerprint -> canonical_kv_key. Each salted entry stores a pointer to canonical key and refcount. On read, resolve pointer to canonical value.
liam: Downsides: extra indirection on hot path and refcount updates under heavy write load. Also heap layout changes.
anna: Alternative: batch-time de-dupe. Before materializing salted keys, the batcher computes content_fingerprint=sha1(prefix) and de-dupes reads within the RPC batch, issuing a single read and then fan-out results. That avoids storage-level dedupe but recovers much of the benefit.
liam: I prototyped batcher de-dupe and saw ~3.7% throughput gain on canary with naive salt.
sylvia: For eviction, propose adding "cohort residency" metric: track number of distinct tenants for each fingerprint and prefer keeping multi-tenant fingerprints longer. Also consider bucketing TTLs by "fanout".
anna: Action items agreed:
- roll back naive tenant-salt flag (anna)
- enable batcher-level de-duplication on canary (liam)
- implement fingerprint->cohort metrics and refcount instrumentation (anna)
- prototype canonical indirection shim in mempool as experiment (sylvia)
- product to consider client opt-in session_affinity token for shareable prefixes
ops-bot: deploy request queued: canary/batcher-dedupe by liam
liam: I'll publish a short wiki blurb about keying tradeoffs and a checklist for future changes.
anna: Filing follow-ups and will attach flame graphs + heap diffs in the PR.
sylvia: Let's sync Thursday to pick an N for cohorted salting if we go that route.
anna: Thanks all. Closing thread for now.
